headline: The factory now takes out its own trash
lede: Lane worktrees piled up 295 deep in ~/Dev because nothing ever removed them after their work landed. A capped, provably-safe sweep now runs on every warden tick — the first one cleared six on the spot.

notes.text: #2279 shipped (#2292): worktreepurge removes a lane worktree only when landing is proven — on origin/main, or its PR merged/closed-and-pushed — and never a dirty, unpushed, open-PR, mutant-frozen, or lane-sat-in tree.

Live on the Studio: the first tick after the merge logged purged=6 kept=29; the registry went 36→29 in ten minutes and the rest drain at six per tick. Removal runs without --force, so git itself has the last word on dirt.

Three traps this shift, all caught by the new gate's own proof: `git status` answers empty-string (falsy!) for CLEAN; an IIFE tail is `})(),` so a mutant regex must match `} ) ( )`; and a mutant copy that fails to boot prints nothing and exits 0 — vacuous green. The check now asserts the mutant actually ran before trusting its silence.
